title: Acts Bible Quiz - Chapter 14
description: Ten questions on Acts 14: Iconium and Lystra, the man who had never walked, and the return through Perga to Antioch.

questions.text: What happened when they spoke in the synagogue at Iconium?
questions.explanation: They spoke in such a way that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.

answers.text: The rulers put them into prison at once
No one in the synagogue would listen to them
They were stoned before they could finish
A great multitude of both Jews and Greeks believed

questions.text: How was the multitude of the city divided?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:4 says part of the multitude sided with the Jews and part with the apostles.

answers.text: Part with the priest of Jupiter and part with Paul
Part sided with the Jews and part with the apostles
The Greeks on one side and the Romans on the other
The rich with the rulers and the poor with Barnabas

questions.text: Where did they flee when a violent attempt was made to stone them?
questions.explanation: They became aware of it and fled to the cities of Lycaonia: Lystra, Derbe and the surrounding region.

answers.text: To Perga and Attalia on the coast
To Antioch and Iconium, where they had been
To Lystra, Derbe and the region around them
To Pisidia and Pamphylia by another road

questions.text: What is said about the man who sat at Lystra?
questions.explanation: He was impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother's womb, who never had walked.

answers.text: He had never walked
He had been blind from birth
He could neither hear nor speak
He was lying sick with a fever

questions.text: What did the man do when Paul said with a loud voice, "Stand upright on your feet!"?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:10 says he leaped up and walked.

answers.text: He stared at Paul without moving
He was carried into the city by friends
He leaped up and walked
He fell down as though he were dead

questions.text: By which names did the multitude at Lystra call Barnabas and Paul?
questions.explanation: They called Barnabas "Jupiter" and Paul "Mercury", because Paul was the chief speaker.

answers.text: Barnabas "Mercury" and Paul "Jupiter"
Barnabas "Jupiter" and Paul "Mercury"
Both of them "sons of the gods"
Barnabas "Artemis" and Paul "Jupiter"

questions.text: What did Barnabas and Paul do when they heard of the sacrifice being prepared?
questions.explanation: The apostles tore their clothes and sprang into the multitude, crying out to them.

answers.text: They tore their clothes and sprang into the multitude
They accepted the oxen and the garlands
They fled out of the city by night
They offered the oxen to the living God

questions.text: How, in Paul's words, had God not left himself without witness?
questions.explanation: He did good and gave them rains from the sky and fruitful seasons, filling their hearts with food and gladness.

answers.text: He sent prophets to every nation
He gave the law to their fathers
He set signs in the sun and the moon
He gave rains from the sky and fruitful seasons

questions.text: What did some Jews from Antioch and Iconium do at Lystra?
questions.explanation: Having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.

answers.text: They stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city
They brought Paul before the magistrates
They burned the books of the sorcerers
They drove Barnabas away by himself

questions.text: What did they do when they had appointed elders in every assembly?
questions.explanation: They prayed with fasting and commended them to the Lord, on whom they had believed.

answers.text: They delivered a letter from the apostles to them
They baptized every one of the disciples again
They prayed with fasting and commended them to the Lord
They laid hands on them and sent them away
